summary: One conditional high, ten medium, four low, and one informational source-review finding were triaged. Fourteen actionable items are tracked. Stateless SAML single-consumption and application-owned IdP group authorization remain documented architecture decisions.

findings.disposition: Make the backend-installed distribution and exact backend wheel authoritative; verify a server-owned complete-wheel SHA-256 before browser installation and make public-index use explicit.
findings.compatibility_note: Custom widgetsets remain supported and continue to be installed on the backend. Private widgets no longer yield priority to an equal public package name and version.

findings.disposition: Preserve stateless SAML browser transactions. Add accurate fresh-client replay coverage and offer a vendor-neutral atomic provider only as an optional strict mode.
findings.existing_mitigation: Signed browser binding, short transaction and assertion expiry, ACS rate limiting, normal-browser replay rejection, secure cookies, and session audience controls.
findings.compatibility_note: No Redis, process memory, sticky routing, or shared store is required. Global single consumption is impossible without shared atomic state.

findings.disposition: Bound capped request-body ingress before BFF execution admission with a separate configurable timeout.
findings.compatibility_note: Only slow request upload is bounded; long-running backend execution retains its separate timeout.

findings.disposition: Bound each blocked streaming response write and release stream admission exactly once after timeout.
findings.compatibility_note: Generators, async generators, yield, moving chunks, and long-running streams remain supported; only a blocked client write is disconnected.

findings.disposition: Bound OAuth initiation and callback rates, exchange concurrency, and provider deadlines; validate application existence before initiation.
findings.compatibility_note: Normal OAuth remains stateless and Redis-free; strict globally atomic callback consumption remains optional.

findings.disposition: Preserve signed IdP group values as authenticated identity claims. Application code, decorators, and policies own authorization and any mapping.
findings.existing_mitigation: An attacker cannot forge signed group values; Pytincture defines no implicit privileged group name.
findings.compatibility_note: SAML_ALLOWED_ROLES is login eligibility, not a filter or framework-owned grant mapping.

findings.disposition: Enforce finite expiration, not-before, issued-at, clock-skew, maximum-age, and maximum-lifetime policy for MCP JWTs.
findings.compatibility_note: Non-expiring tokens require migration or an explicit compatibility setting; secure production mode requires bounded tokens.

findings.disposition: Use host-prefixed HTTPS production authentication cookies and separate unprefixed HTTP development cookie names.
findings.compatibility_note: Production users may need one fresh login. Local HTTP development remains supported.

findings.disposition: Cache bounded per-application graph snapshots with secure automatic invalidation and early impossible-operation rejection.
findings.compatibility_note: The process-local cache remains stateless and disposable, and same-name development edits must invalidate.

findings.disposition: Cache public-asset authorization and add configurable admission, byte, and blocked-write limits.
findings.compatibility_note: Public assets remain unauthenticated. Large media may need raised limits or external object storage; same-name changes remain visible.

findings.disposition: Make replay-refill quota accounting denial-safe through ordered short-circuiting or transactional reservations.
findings.compatibility_note: Accepted requests are unchanged and replay refill remains disabled by default.

findings.disposition: Key only isolated-process fairness to an HMAC-protected stable authenticated identity and use generous configurable concurrency with fair queuing.
findings.compatibility_note: Ordinary cooperative async BFF calls and normal async multitasking are not limited by this control.

findings.disposition: Expose immutable Microsoft identity clearly, document it for sensitive authorization, and warn when production admission relies only on mutable email.
findings.compatibility_note: Email and domain admission remain available for simple applications.

findings.disposition: Equalize oversized-password failure work and transparently migrate successful bcrypt verification to Argon2id when supported.
findings.compatibility_note: Password values and the login API do not change.

findings.disposition: Compare exact runtime type and value for Literal validation and handle None explicitly.
findings.compatibility_note: Only JSON values whose type violates the declared annotation are rejected.

findings.disposition: Add optional production controls for API documentation and detailed readiness while preserving a minimal public health endpoint.
findings.compatibility_note: Development defaults remain convenient and no forced behavior change is required.

accepted_residual_risks.reason: Immediate fleet-wide revocation of a copied stateless cookie requires shared mutable state. Absolute expiry, key rotation, Secure and HttpOnly cookies, and application audience restrictions remain the no-store controls.
Hosted service mode uses the vendored runtime. External runtime mode is an explicit application trust decision and its bootstrap scripts retain SRI.
A policy hook returning None retains the documented allow compatibility contract; application-owned conditional policies must explicitly deny or raise.
Python threads cannot be killed safely. Isolated-process mode provides bounded killable containment for trusted non-streaming work that requires hard termination.
Pytincture authenticates selected browser packages but does not sandbox separately maintained widgetset implementations.
